title: Ezekiel 37 — The valley of dry bones and the two sticks

paragraphs.text: הָיְתָ֣ה עָלַי֮ יַד־יְהוָה֒ וַיּוֹצִאֵ֤נִי בְר֙וּחַ֙ יְהוָ֔ה וַיְנִיחֵ֖נִי בְּת֣וֹךְ הַבִּקְעָ֑ה וְהִ֖יא מְלֵאָ֥ה עֲצָמֽוֹת׃

i18n.en: The hand of YHWH was upon me, and he brought me out by the ruach of YHWH and set me down in the middle of the valley — and it was full of bones.

notes.official: **The chapter opens with the prophetic-onset formula.** *Hayetah alai yad-YHWH* — *the hand of YHWH was upon me* — the same formula as 1:3, 3:14, 8:1, 33:22, 40:1. The prophet is taken-hold-of. // *Vayyotzieni b'ruach YHWH* — *and he brought me out by the ruach of YHWH*. The *ruach* here is the *animating-directive* force of the Ezekiel vision-sequences (cf. 3:12, 3:14, 8:3, 11:1, 11:24, 43:5) — the same vocabulary that runs through ch 1 (*ruach* in the chayyot, *ruach* in the wheels) and ch 10. The prophet is *transported* by the ruach. // *Vayynicheni b'tokh ha-biq'ah* — *and set me down in the middle of the valley*. The verb *vayynicheni* (from *nuach* — *to rest, settle, place*) is the same root as the ark coming-to-rest on the mountains of Ararat (Gen 8:4) and as Noah's name. The prophet is *placed*, deliberately positioned. // *Biq'ah* — *valley, plain*. The same noun as Gen 11:2 (the *biq'ah* in the land of Shinar where Babel was built) and Isa 40:4 (the valleys-to-be-raised). The chapter places the bone-field in a *biq'ah*, an open flat space — the topographic feature that historically hosted Mesopotamian construction projects, military encampments, and now this bone-yard. The vision happens on a *staging-area*.

paragraphs.text: וְהֶעֱבִירַ֥נִי עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם סָבִ֣יב ׀ סָבִ֑יב וְהִנֵּ֨ה רַבּ֤וֹת מְאֹד֙ עַל־פְּנֵ֣י הַבִּקְעָ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֖ה יְבֵשׁ֥וֹת מְאֹֽד׃

i18n.en: He led me past them all around — and behold, they were very many on the face of the valley, and behold, they were very dry.

notes.official: **The reconnaissance.** The prophet is led *saviv saviv* — *round and round* — past the bones in a methodical survey. Two facts establish: *rabbot me'od* (very many) and *yeveshot me'od* (very dry). The dry-bones identification is the chapter's keyword — *atzamot yeveshot* will recur as the technical descriptor (37:4, 11). // The doubled *me'od* (very many / very dry) emphasizes the magnitude. *Atzamot* (עֲצָמוֹת, plural of *etzem* — bone) is the standard Hebrew word for bones — both the skeletal-anatomical sense and the metaphorical (*atzem* — substance, essence). The bones are *yeveshot* (dry) — the verb root *yavesh* (to dry up, wither) — denoting both the literal desiccated state and the metaphorical hopelessness.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י בֶּן־אָדָ֕ם הֲתִחְיֶ֖ינָה הָעֲצָמ֣וֹת הָאֵ֑לֶּה וָאֹמַ֕ר אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה אַתָּ֥ה יָדָֽעְתָּ׃

i18n.en: He said to me, "Son of human, can these bones live?" And I said, "Lord YHWH, you know."

notes.official: **The address: *Ben-adam*.** *Ben-adam* (בֶּן־אָדָם) — *son of human / son of Adam* — is the prophet's standard appellation throughout Ezekiel (it appears 93 times across the book, more than any other Hebrew Bible figure). The compound combines *ben* (son) + *adam* (human/Adam). The Hebrew Bible elsewhere uses *ben-adam* as a poetic-emphatic for *mortal* (Ps 8:5, 80:18, 144:3; Job 25:6, 35:8); the Aramaic equivalent *bar-enash* in Dan 7:13 will become the New Testament *ho huios tou anthrōpou* — *the son of man* — Jesus' self-designation. // The chapter's framing is precise: the prophet (a human, a *ben-adam*) is asked about the prospects of *human* bones. The question is anthropological-categorial. // The prophet's response — *Adonai YHWH attah yada'ta* — *Lord YHWH, you know* — is properly humble: he does not commit either way. The question's answer is reserved for the one who can know.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י הִנָּבֵ֖א עַל־הָעֲצָמ֣וֹת הָאֵ֑לֶּה וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם הָעֲצָמוֹת֙ הַיְבֵשׁ֔וֹת שִׁמְע֖וּ דְּבַר־יְהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: He said to me, "Prophesy upon these bones, and say to them: dry bones, hear the word of YHWH!"

notes.official: **The prophet is to address the bones directly.** *Dvar-YHWH* — *the word of YHWH* — is the standard prophetic-formula term for divine communication. The chapter is staging a remarkable inversion: the bones are being addressed *as if they could hear*. The chapter's whole drama is whether dead matter can receive the word.

paragraphs.text: כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה לָעֲצָמ֖וֹת הָאֵ֑לֶּה הִנֵּ֨ה אֲנִ֜י מֵבִ֥יא בָכֶ֛ם ר֖וּחַ וִחְיִיתֶֽם׃

i18n.en: Thus says the Lord YHWH to these bones: behold, I am bringing ruach into you, and you shall live.

notes.official: **The first announcement.** *Hinneh ani mevi vakhem ruach v'chyitem* — *behold, I am bringing ruach into you, and you shall live*. The verb *bo'* in hiphil (*mevi* — *bringing-in*) is causative-introductive. The *ruach* is to be *introduced into* the bones; the result will be *chayyim* (living). The bones are being told the procedure in advance, and the procedure has two named stages: structural-assembly (vv 6-8) and animating-introduction (vv 9-10).

paragraphs.text: וְנָתַתִּי֩ עֲלֵיכֶ֨ם גִּדִ֜ים וְֽהַעֲלֵתִ֧י עֲלֵיכֶ֣ם בָּשָׂ֗ר וְקָרַמְתִּ֤י עֲלֵיכֶם֙ ע֔וֹר וְנָתַתִּ֥י בָכֶ֛ם ר֖וּחַ וִחְיִיתֶ֑ם וִידַעְתֶּ֖ם כִּֽי־אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: I will put sinews upon you, raise flesh upon you, cover you with skin, and put ruach in you — and you shall live, and you shall know that I am YHWH.

notes.official: **The staged-construction sequence, fully named.** The chapter lists the procedure in four explicit stages: // 1. *Gidim* (גִּדִים) — *sinews / tendons / connective tissue*. The structural connecting-elements that bind the bone-framework. // 2. *Basar* (בָּשָׂר) — *flesh* — the soft tissue raised *upon* (*ha'aleti aleichem*) the bone-and-sinew framework. // 3. *`Or* (עוֹר) — *skin* — applied to *cover* (*qaramti* — from *qaram*, a hapax verb meaning *to overlay/cover-with-membrane*). // 4. *Ruach* (רוּחַ) — the animating-introduced last, after the body is assembled. // The sequence is **technically-anatomically ordered**: structural framework → connective tissue → soft tissue → integument → animation. This is the canonical sequence of biological assembly described in step-by-step procedural language. // The Wheel of Heaven lens reads this verse with attention to the Raëlian canon's reading of Ezek 37 in *Extra-Terrestrials Took Me To Their Planet* — the canon identifies this passage as the description of a biological-creation procedure: the same staged-construction the Elohim are said to have used to bring humanity into being. The chapter's own vocabulary — *gidim / basar / `or / ruach* in that order — is procedurally precise and matches the technical-sequential description of body-assembly. The lens lives in the recognition of what the chapter's procedural vocabulary specifies; the translation preserves the procedural language.

paragraphs.text: וְנִבֵּ֖אתִי כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר צֻוֵּ֑יתִי וַֽיְהִי־ק֤וֹל כְּהִנָּֽבְאִי֙ וְהִנֵּה־רַ֔עַשׁ וַתִּקְרְב֣וּ עֲצָמ֔וֹת עֶ֖צֶם אֶל־עַצְמֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: I prophesied as I had been commanded; and as I prophesied, there was a sound — and behold, a rattling — and the bones drew near, bone to its bone.

notes.official: **The first stage is heard before it is seen.** *Vay'hi qol k'hinnav'i v'hinneh-ra'ash* — *and there was a sound as I prophesied, and behold, a rattling*. Two distinct auditory events: a *qol* (sound, voice) and a *ra'ash* (rattling, shaking, quaking — the same word used for earthquakes). The chapter is describing the bone-reassembly *acoustically* — bones moving, drawing together, contacting each other make sound. // *Vatiqr'vu atzamot etzem el-atzmo* — *the bones drew near, bone to its bone*. The verb *qarav* (draw near) and the distributive construction *etzem el-atzmo* (bone to its bone) name the precise reassembly: each bone moves to its matching anatomical position. The reassembly is *correct* — bones go to the bones they belong with, not at random.

paragraphs.text: וְרָאִ֜יתִי וְהִנֵּֽה־עֲלֵיהֶ֤ם גִּדִים֙ וּבָשָׂ֣ר עָלָ֔ה וַיִּקְרַ֧ם עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם ע֖וֹר מִלְמָ֑עְלָה וְר֖וּחַ אֵ֥ין בָּהֶֽם׃

i18n.en: I looked, and behold — sinews were upon them, flesh came up, and skin covered them from above. But ruach was not in them.

notes.official: **The body is assembled — but not yet living.** The verse reports the procedural completion of stages 2-4 (sinews, flesh, skin) and the absent stage 5 (ruach). *V'ruach ein bahem* — *but ruach was not in them*. The bodies are anatomically complete — bones, sinews, flesh, skin, in the correct sequence — but they are not living. The animating principle has not yet been introduced. // The two-stage structure of the procedure is now visible: the *body* is assembled by one prophetic word (v4-7); the *animation* will be introduced by a second prophetic word (v9-10). The chapter is separating *somatic-assembly* from *animation* — they are distinct procedures requiring distinct interventions.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י הִנָּבֵ֖א אֶל־הָר֑וּחַ הִנָּבֵ֣א בֶן־אָ֠דָם וְאָמַרְתָּ֨ אֶל־הָר֜וּחַ כֹּֽה־אָמַ֣ר ׀ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה מֵאַרְבַּ֤ע רוּחוֹת֙ בֹּ֣אִי הָר֔וּחַ וּפְחִ֛י בַּהֲרוּגִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה וְיִֽחְיֽוּ׃

i18n.en: He said to me, "Prophesy to the ruach — prophesy, son of human — and say to the ruach: thus says the Lord YHWH: from the four ruchot, come, ruach, and breathe into these slain, that they may live."

notes.official: **The second prophetic word — addressed to the ruach itself.** *Hinnave el-ha-ruach* — *prophesy to the ruach*. The prophet is to address not the bones but the *ruach* — and to summon it *me-arba ruchot* — *from the four ruchot*. // The construction is precise. *Arba ruchot* is the Hebrew Bible's phrase for *the four winds / the four directions* (cf. Jer 49:36, Zech 2:6, Dan 7:2, Dan 8:8, Dan 11:4). The *ruach* (singular) is to come from *the four ruchot* (plural, the cardinal directions). The chapter is staging a *summoning* of the animating principle from the four corners. // *Puchi ba-harugim ha-eleh v'yichyu* — *and breathe into these slain that they may live*. The verb *puach* (פּוּחַ) — *to blow, breathe* — is the same verb used in Gen 2:7 for YHWH-Elohim breathing the *nishmat chayyim* (breath of life) into the human's nostrils. The chapter is verbally citing the Gen 2:7 creation-of-adam-from-dust procedure — the bones-from-the-valley are being treated to the same procedure that originally animated the first *adam*. // *Harugim* (הֲרוּגִים) — *slain, killed* — names the bones in their pre-history: they are the dead, the killed. The chapter is staging a *resurrection-procedure* not as a generic miracle but as the re-application of the original animation-procedure of Gen 2:7.

paragraphs.text: וְהִנַּבֵּ֖אתִי כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוָּ֑נִי וַתָּבוֹא֩ בָהֶ֨ם הָר֜וּחַ וַיִּֽחְי֗וּ וַיַּֽעַמְדוּ֙ עַל־רַגְלֵיהֶ֔ם חַ֖יִל גָּד֥וֹל מְאֹד־מְאֹֽד׃

i18n.en: I prophesied as he had commanded me, and the ruach came into them, and they lived, and they stood up on their feet — an exceedingly great army.

notes.official: **The completion.** The fifth stage executes: *vatavo vahem ha-ruach vayichyu* — *and the ruach came into them, and they lived*. The verbal sequence is staccato — three perfect-consecutive verbs in quick succession (*va-niba'eti / vatavo / vayichyu / vaya'amdu*) — match the procedure-completion register. // *Vaya'amdu al-raglehem* — *and they stood up on their feet*. The bodies are now functional — they stand, they have postural control. *Chayil gadol me'od me'od* — *an exceedingly great army*. The standard reading is military-eschatological: a vast restored population, framed as an army for the eschatological restoration. The doubled *me'od* (very-very) emphasizes the scale. // The chapter has now completed the staged-construction-and-animation in seven verses (4-10): two prophetic words, five biological-procedure stages (bones-assembled, sinews, flesh, skin, ruach), producing a vast living population from a valley of dry remains.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֮ אֵלַי֒ בֶּן־אָדָ֕ם הָעֲצָמ֣וֹת הָאֵ֔לֶּה כָּל־בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל הֵ֑מָּה הִנֵּ֣ה אֹמְרִ֗ים יָבְשׁ֧וּ עַצְמוֹתֵ֛ינוּ וְאָבְדָ֥ה תִקְוָתֵ֖נוּ נִגְזַ֥רְנוּ לָֽנוּ׃

i18n.en: He said to me, "Son of human, these bones are the whole house of Israel. Behold, they are saying: 'Our bones are dried up, our hope is lost, we are cut off.'"

notes.official: **The interpretation: the bones are the whole house of Israel.** The chapter pivots from the staged procedure to its meaning. *Ha-atzamot ha-eleh kol bet Yisrael hemmah* — *these bones are the whole house of Israel*. The vision is now declared to be *about* the exiled, despairing Israelite community. The chapter has the people quoting their own despair: *yav'shu atzmotenu, avdah tiqvatenu, nigzarnu lanu* — *our bones are dried up, our hope is lost, we are cut off*. // The chapter is making a strong textual move: it stages a *biological-procedural vision* (vv 1-10) and then names that procedure as the metaphor for *the restoration of an exiled people*. The Wheel of Heaven reading holds both registers simultaneously: the chapter is *about* the restoration of Israel from exile (the explicit interpretation v11-14) AND it stages a *procedural-technical* vision the Raëlian canon reads as a literal description of biological-creation procedure. Both readings are textually present; neither cancels the other.

paragraphs.text: לָכֵן֩ הִנָּבֵ֨א וְאָמַרְתָּ֜ אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם כֹּֽה־אָמַר֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ הִנֵּה֩ אֲנִ֨י פֹתֵ֜חַ אֶת־קִבְרֽוֹתֵיכֶ֗ם וְהַעֲלֵיתִ֥י אֶתְכֶ֛ם מִקִּבְרוֹתֵיכֶ֖ם עַמִּ֑י וְהֵבֵאתִ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם אֶל־אַדְמַ֥ת יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: Therefore prophesy and say to them: thus says the Lord YHWH: behold, I am opening your graves and bringing you up out of your graves, my people, and I will bring you into the land of Israel.

notes.official: **The grave-opening promise.** *Hinneh ani fote'ach et-qivrotekhem* — *behold, I am opening your graves*. The verb *fatach* (open) in present-participial *poteach* (currently-opening) — the action is *in process*. The graves are being opened, the people raised up, brought back to Israel's land. // The chapter expands the vision's scope: where vv 5-10 were a procedure on bones-in-a-valley, v12 is a procedure on *graves* — Israel's dispersed, buried dead are being raised. The shift from valley-of-bones to graves-being-opened broadens the imagery beyond a single battlefield-aftermath to the diaspora-mass-dead more generally.

paragraphs.text: וִֽידַעְתֶּ֖ם כִּֽי־אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֑ה בְּפִתְחִ֣י אֶת־קִבְרֽוֹתֵיכֶ֗ם וּבְהַעֲלוֹתִ֥י אֶתְכֶ֛ם מִקִּבְרוֹתֵיכֶ֖ם עַמִּֽי׃

i18n.en: You shall know that I am YHWH when I open your graves and bring you up out of your graves, my people.

paragraphs.text: וְנָתַתִּ֨י רוּחִ֤י בָכֶם֙ וִחְיִיתֶ֔ם וְהִנַּחְתִּ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם עַל־אַדְמַתְכֶ֑ם וִידַעְתֶּ֤ם כִּי־אֲנִ֤י יְהוָ֤ה דִּבַּ֙רְתִּי֙ וְעָשִׂ֔יתִי נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: I will put my ruach in you, and you shall live; and I will set you upon your own land. Then you shall know that I — YHWH — have spoken and have done it, declares YHWH.

notes.official: **The closure of the vision-and-interpretation.** *V'natati ruchi bakhem v'chyitem* — *I will put my ruach in you, and you shall live*. The chapter ends its first major unit by re-citing the procedure: *ruach in / living out*. The vision's signature move — the introduction of ruach as the animating principle — is now applied not just to the bones-on-the-floor but to *the entire dispersed people*. // *Dibbarti v'asiti* — *I have spoken and have done it*. The verbal pair frames the chapter's claim: prophetic word and divine action are coextensive. What was prophesied is what is done.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃

i18n.en: The word of YHWH came to me, saying:

notes.official: **Transitional formula.** The standard Ezekiel prophetic-word-formula introduces the chapter's second major unit (vv 15-28): the parable of the two sticks. The bone-valley narrative is complete; what follows is a sign-act that interprets the restoration as the *reunification* of the divided kingdom.

paragraphs.text: וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן־אָדָ֗ם קַח־לְךָ֙ עֵ֣ץ אֶחָ֔ד וּכְתֹ֤ב עָלָיו֙ לִֽיהוּדָ֔ה וְלִבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל חֲבֵרָ֑ו וּלְקַח֙ עֵ֣ץ אֶחָ֔ד וּכְת֣וֹב עָלָ֗יו לְיוֹסֵף֙ עֵ֣ץ אֶפְרַ֔יִם וְכָל־בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל חֲבֵרָֽיו׃

i18n.en: And you, son of human, take a single stick and write on it: 'For Judah, and for the sons of Israel his companions.' Then take another stick and write on it: 'For Joseph — the stick of Ephraim — and for all the house of Israel his companions.'

notes.official: **The two-sticks sign-act.** Ezekiel is to take two sticks and label them with the two political halves of the divided kingdom: *Yehudah* (Judah, the southern kingdom with Jerusalem as capital, the David-Solomonic dynasty) and *Yosef / Efrayim* (Joseph / Ephraim, the northern kingdom — the ten tribes who broke off after Solomon's death and were taken into Assyrian exile in 722 BCE). The chapter is performing a *prophetic sign-act* — a physical demonstration in front of an audience — that visually predicts political unification. // *Yosef-Efrayim*: Ephraim was the dominant tribe of the Joseph line in the northern kingdom; the kingdom-of-the-north is alternately called *Yosef* or *Efrayim* in Hebrew Bible prophetic literature. // The sign-act picks up an older prophetic-tradition pattern (cf. Isa 8:1-4, Jer 13:1-11, Jer 18:1-12) where the prophet enacts the message physically before announcing it verbally.

paragraphs.text: וְקָרַ֨ב אֹתָ֜ם אֶחָ֧ד אֶל־אֶחָ֛ד לְךָ֖ לְעֵ֣ץ אֶחָ֑ד וְהָי֥וּ לַאֲחָדִ֖ים בְּיָדֶֽךָ׃

i18n.en: Bring them near, one to one, for yourself into a single stick — and they shall become one in your hand.

notes.official: **The fusion act.** The chapter does not specify the mechanism — Ezekiel is to *bring near, one to one*, and the sticks *become one*. The Hebrew uses *qarav* (the same verb as in v7 *vatiqrvu atzamot* — the bones drew near to one another). The verbal echo links the bones-reassembling-by-themselves moment (v7) to the sticks-becoming-one moment (v17): both are described as a *drawing-near* that produces unity.

paragraphs.text: וְכַֽאֲשֶׁר֙ יֹאמְר֣וּ אֵלֶ֔יךָ בְּנֵ֥י עַמְּךָ֖ לֵאמֹ֑ר הֲלֽוֹא־תַגִּ֥יד לָ֖נוּ מָה־אֵ֥לֶּה לָּֽךְ׃

i18n.en: When the people of your community say to you, "Will you not tell us what these mean for you?" —

paragraphs.text: דַּבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם כֹּֽה־אָמַר֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ הִנֵּה֩ אֲנִ֨י לֹקֵ֜חַ אֶת־עֵ֤ץ יוֹסֵף֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּיַד־אֶפְרַ֔יִם וְשִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל חֲבֵרָ֑ו וְנָתַתִּי֩ אוֹתָ֨ם עָלָ֜יו אֶת־עֵ֣ץ יְהוּדָ֗ה וַֽעֲשִׂיתִם֙ לְעֵ֣ץ אֶחָ֔ד וְהָי֥וּ אֶחָ֖ד בְּיָדִֽי׃

i18n.en: Say to them: thus says the Lord YHWH: behold, I am taking the stick of Joseph — which is in the hand of Ephraim, and the tribes of Israel his companions — and I will lay them with it — the stick of Judah — and I will make them into one stick, and they shall be one in my hand.

paragraphs.text: וְהָי֨וּ הָעֵצִ֜ים אֲ‍ֽשֶׁר־תִּכְתֹּ֧ב עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם בְּיָדְךָ֖ לְעֵינֵיהֶֽם׃

i18n.en: The sticks on which you write shall be in your hand before their eyes.

paragraphs.text: וְדַבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם כֹּֽה־אָמַר֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ הִנֵּ֨ה אֲנִ֤י לֹקֵ֙חַ֙ אֶת־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִבֵּ֥ין הַגּוֹיִ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָֽלְכוּ־שָׁ֑ם וְקִבַּצְתִּ֤י אֹתָם֙ מִסָּבִ֔יב וְהֵבֵאתִ֥י אוֹתָ֖ם אֶל־אַדְמָתָֽם׃

i18n.en: Say to them: thus says the Lord YHWH: behold, I am taking the sons of Israel from among the nations where they have gone, and I will gather them from all around and bring them to their own land.

notes.official: **The political-historical promise.** The two-sticks parable is now applied: the unification will happen by *gathering the dispersed* (*qibbatzti* — from *qabatz*, *to gather*) from among the nations. The verse picks up the standard prophetic-restoration vocabulary (cf. Deut 30:3-5, Jer 23:3, Isa 11:12). The reunification of north and south is part of a broader diaspora-ingathering.

paragraphs.text: וְעָשִׂ֣יתִי אֹ֠תָם לְג֨וֹי אֶחָ֤ד בָּאָ֙רֶץ֙ בְּהָרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וּמֶ֧לֶךְ אֶחָ֛ד יִֽהְיֶ֥ה לְכֻלָּ֖ם לְמֶ֑לֶךְ וְלֹ֤א יִֽהְיוּ־עוֹד֙ לִשְׁנֵ֣י גוֹיִ֔ם וְלֹ֨א יֵחָ֧צוּ ע֛וֹד לִשְׁתֵּ֥י מַמְלָכ֖וֹת עֽוֹד׃

i18n.en: I will make them into one nation in the land, in the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king for all of them. They shall no longer be two nations, and they shall no longer be divided into two kingdoms anymore.

notes.official: ***Goy echad*** — *one nation*. ***Melekh echad*** — *one king*. The chapter's final political vision: a single Israelite polity under a single monarchy. The chapter has carefully not yet named the king — verse 24 will identify him as *David my servant*. // The verse uses the Hebrew Bible's standard term for Israelite political division: *shenei goyim* (*two nations*) referring to the post-Solomonic split between the northern kingdom (Israel/Joseph/Ephraim) and the southern kingdom (Judah). The chapter is promising the undoing of the 922 BCE political division — a unification that did not historically occur (the northern kingdom was destroyed in 722 BCE, the southern in 587 BCE; the post-exilic restoration covered only Judah).

paragraphs.text: וְלֹ֧א יִֽטַמְּא֣וּ ע֗וֹד בְּגִלּֽוּלֵיהֶם֙ וּבְשִׁקּ֣וּצֵיהֶ֔ם וּבְכֹ֖ל פִּשְׁעֵיהֶ֑ם וְהוֹשַׁעְתִּ֣י אֹתָ֗ם מִכֹּ֤ל מוֹשְׁבֹֽתֵיהֶם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָטְא֣וּ בָהֶ֔ם וְטִהַרְתִּ֖י אוֹתָ֑ם וְהָיוּ־לִ֣י לְעָ֔ם וַאֲנִ֕י אֶהְיֶ֥ה לָהֶ֖ם לֵאלֹהִֽים׃

i18n.en: They shall no longer defile themselves with their idols, their detestable things, and any of their transgressions; I will save them from all their dwellings where they have sinned, and I will purify them; and they shall be my people, and I will be their Elohim.

notes.official: **The covenant formula.** *V'hayu li l'am va-ani ehyeh lahem l'Elohim* — *and they shall be my people, and I will be their Elohim*. The two-sided covenant formula appears repeatedly across the Hebrew Bible (Ex 6:7, Lev 26:12, Jer 7:23, Jer 11:4, Jer 24:7, Jer 30:22, Jer 31:33, Ezek 11:20, 14:11, 36:28, 37:23, 37:27; Zech 8:8). It compresses the entire covenant relation into a chiasmic exchange of belonging. // The WoH translation preserves *Elohim* (not 'God') per the project's convention (see [`elohim-as-translation`](/wiki/elohim/)).

paragraphs.text: וְעַבְדִּ֤י דָוִד֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם וְרוֹעֶ֥ה אֶחָ֖ד יִהְיֶ֣ה לְכֻלָּ֑ם וּבְמִשְׁפָּטַ֣י יֵלֵ֔כוּ וְחֻקּוֹתַ֥י יִשְׁמְר֖וּ וְעָשׂ֥וּ אוֹתָֽם׃

i18n.en: My servant David shall be king over them, and there shall be one shepherd for all of them; they shall walk in my ordinances and keep my statutes and do them.

notes.official: ***Avdi David melekh aleihem*** — *my servant David shall be king over them*. The single-king of v22 is now named: *David*. The historical David died in ~970 BCE; the chapter is forecasting either a literal resurrection of David, or — more standard in Hebrew Bible prophetic-restoration vocabulary — a Davidic-line ruler (a *new David*, descended from David's line). The chapter is invoking the *messianic-Davidic* tradition that runs through Hebrew Bible eschatological prophecy (Isa 9:6-7, 11:1-10, Jer 23:5-6, 30:9, Hos 3:5, Amos 9:11, Mic 5:2). // *Ro'eh echad* — *one shepherd* — picks up the shepherd-king imagery of Ezek 34, with David as the messianic-shepherd-figure.

paragraphs.text: וְיָשְׁב֣וּ עַל־הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֤ר נָתַ֙תִּי֙ לְעַבְדִּ֣י לְיַֽעֲקֹ֔ב אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָֽשְׁבוּ־בָ֖הּ אֲבֽוֹתֵיכֶ֑ם וְיָשְׁב֣וּ עָלֶ֡יהָ הֵ֠מָּה וּבְנֵיהֶ֞ם וּבְנֵ֤י בְנֵיהֶם֙ עַד־עוֹלָ֔ם וְדָוִ֣ד עַבְדִּ֔י נָשִׂ֥יא לָהֶ֖ם לְעוֹלָֽם׃

i18n.en: They shall dwell on the land that I gave to my servant Jacob, where your fathers dwelt — they and their children and their children's children shall dwell on it forever; and David my servant shall be their prince forever.

paragraphs.text: וְכָרַתִּ֤י לָהֶם֙ בְּרִ֣ית שָׁל֔וֹם בְּרִ֥ית עוֹלָ֖ם יִהְיֶ֣ה אוֹתָ֑ם וּנְתַתִּים֙ וְהִרְבֵּיתִ֣י אוֹתָ֔ם וְנָתַתִּ֧י אֶת־מִקְדָּשִׁ֛י בְּתוֹכָ֖ם לְעוֹלָֽם׃

i18n.en: I will cut a covenant of peace with them — it shall be an everlasting covenant with them — and I will establish them and multiply them, and I will set my sanctuary in their midst forever.

notes.official: ***Brit shalom, brit olam*** — *covenant of peace, everlasting covenant*. The chapter is naming a *new* covenant — the Hebrew Bible distinguishes covenant-of-peace and everlasting-covenant from the Sinaitic-Mosaic covenant (cf. Isa 54:10, Jer 31:31-34). The post-restoration covenant is permanent (*olam* — forever, indefinite duration). // *Et-miqdashi b'tokham* — *my sanctuary in their midst*. The chapter is promising a new Temple — one that will not require a future kavod-departure scene like Ezekiel 10. The end-state of the restoration is YHWH's permanent dwelling in the midst of Israel.

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֤ה מִשְׁכָּנִי֙ עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם וְהָיִ֥יתִי לָהֶ֖ם לֵֽאלֹהִ֑ים וְהֵ֖מָּה יִֽהְיוּ־לִ֥י לְעָֽם׃

i18n.en: My dwelling shall be above them; I will be their Elohim, and they shall be my people.

notes.official: ***Mishkani aleihem*** — *my dwelling above them*. *Mishkan* (מִשְׁכָּן) — *tabernacle, dwelling-place* — is the technical term for the portable wilderness sanctuary of Exodus (Ex 25-31, 35-40). The chapter is naming the eschatological-restoration sanctuary as a *mishkan* — a *dwelling-place* over the people. The chapter's final covenantal vision: YHWH dwelling among the unified, restored people, in a permanent mishkan, with David as the prince and one shepherd for all.

paragraphs.text: וְיָֽדְעוּ֙ הַגּוֹיִ֔ם כִּ֚י אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה מְקַדֵּ֖שׁ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל בִּהְי֧וֹת מִקְדָּשִׁ֛י בְּתוֹכָ֖ם לְעוֹלָֽם׃

i18n.en: Then the nations shall know that I am YHWH, who sanctifies Israel — when my sanctuary is in their midst forever.

notes.official: **The closing recognition-formula.** *V'yadu ha-goyim ki ani YHWH* — *and the nations shall know that I am YHWH*. The Hebrew Bible's standard *recognition-formula* (occurs in slight variations across Ezekiel ~70 times) closes the chapter. The witnesses are the *goyim* — the nations, the non-Israelite peoples — who will recognize YHWH precisely by seeing the eschatological-restoration realized. // The chapter closes the entire two-part vision (valley-of-bones-and-restoration of vv 1-14 + two-sticks-reunification of vv 15-28) on a future-tense recognition: the goyim will come to know what YHWH has been doing through what they will see.
